experiment: C4 two-level recursive Canaria composition tree
interpretation: After the six-local-candidate cluster was jointly adapted and frozen, both recursive compilation levels used only adapted-cluster or pair-cluster behavior as fit targets; original teacher a6 was not used.
The second recursive level increased original-teacher NMSE relative to one-level recursion in all 3 seeds, but the increase was modest: 1.054x, 1.090x, and 1.080x; geometric mean 1.0745x.
The two-level final's geometric-mean NMSE ratio relative to direct original-teacher recompilation was 1.4625x across the 3 exploratory seeds.
Mean validation accuracy was identical for one-level and two-level recursive singles at 0.96049, versus 0.96420 for direct original recompilation.
The pair-cluster intermediate itself remained close to the adapted-six teacher and did not show catastrophic compounding.
C4 supports a hypothesis of controlled error accumulation across two recursive compilation levels, but fresh confirmatory seeds are required before any recursive-depth public claim.
